title: A Following Wind
summary: No cargo, no deadline you didn't agree to, no faction watching: just the flats grand loop. East gate chalk, up to the dune overlook, back through the moorage rigging, swing the water tower, carve the old pan, and home — five gates of clean salt and nothing to prove. Ketch will be on the radio the whole way. He's worse than weather.

objectives.label: Stage at the east gate chalk
The grand loop: overlook → moorage → water tower → old pan → home

offer.text: Kid. You've been hauling and dodging and outrunning everything this desert throws, and I realised nobody's ever sent you out to just *ride*. That's a training failure and I'm correcting it. The grand loop: five gates, my clock, your line. Prize is a tin of the good tea and me never shutting up on the radio.

Rules: there aren't any. Boost when it feels right, drift when the salt says so, and if you find yourself grinning inside the helmet — that's the mission. Old couriers called this one 'a following wind'. You'll see why at the pan.

accept.text: Radio check. I'll be your weather, your crowd, and your conscience. Gate one is the climb — don't boost the dune face, float it. Two is the rigging at the moorage; mind the mast cables, they'll shave a fin if you get greedy. Three, the tower, is where you learn what a wide line costs. Four's the pan. Nothing at the pan but room.
So no cargo, no clock that means anything, and a full commentary track from a man who once called a sandstorm 'textured'. This is the best job I've ever taken. Staging now.

Word of warning from the board: it's not a Guild posting, so if you plant the bike it's not covered. Ketch, the garage's liability and the garage's *sentiment* both sign my paperwork conceptually. Have fun, courier. That's an instruction.

complete.text: Clock stopped. Line was — kid, that drift off the pan into the east gate was *criminal*, and I mean that as the highest compliment this garage issues. The Wren's purring in a key I haven't heard since Old Bahro's day. That's what riding's for. Remember the feeling; the desert'll spend the rest of your career trying to take it back.

The loop's yours now. Any time the book's full of crates and factions and cylinders that hum, you run those five gates and remember: the fastest thing out here isn't a storm, it's a courier with nothing to prove and a following wind. Flat salt to you, kid. That's the whole blessing.
Still grinning. If Tamsin asks what I was doing, tell her I was 'maintaining morale infrastructure'. She'll find a form for it.
